_about: City planner programs (Jordan, 28 Nov 2026: every deck is a working city built around its purpose; every building has a purpose and a place). A program says what a district must have to do its job. tools/city_planner.py checks a district's data against its program, lists what is missing, and places the missing pieces in free land as 'proposed'. Rules marked 'assumption' are planner guesses for Jordan to confirm. Distances are metric here (km); the report shows US units first.

3.purpose: Social life city; new players start in their quarters here

5.purpose: Hangar City: the hangar and transport city for everyone on the ship, coming and going

D5-port-of-arrivals.purpose: The main way in and out of the whole ship. People arrive and leave here, whether military, commercial or community, so the outer hull needs many doors, big and small, and the port needs high security.

implied_doors.Arrival hangar: canon dock door 131 x 33 ft (40 x 10 m), Jordan 21 Nov 2026

door_classes.name: Yard lock (ships to the repair yards)
Small craft locks (skiffs and private runabouts)
Guard and government berths (security, military and official craft)
door_classes.why: Jordan: doors for military as well as commercial and community traffic. The big warships use the Cruiser Docks; the Port needs its own berths for patrol cutters, military transports and official arrivals, one at each end of the hull front.

door_classes.name: Crew airlocks (small walk-through doors for crews, inspectors and suited work)
door_classes.why: Every 1,640 ft (500 m) frame of hull is its own sealable pressure zone (Ship Reference 5), so each needs a small door that does not need a ship-sized door to open.

door_classes.name: Freight gate (cargo ships)
door_classes.why: Cargo now comes in through the berths and goes by Dock Road to Cargo Customs. A gate of its own beside Freight (P4) would need hull frontage that is all in use. Left for Jordan.

response.name: Fire and rescue
response.why: Airport fire rules: crash rescue reaches any point of a runway in 3 minutes, about 1 mile (1.6 km).

response.name: Police and port security
response.why: Every hull door is a way into the ship; a police post within about a mile can reach it in minutes.

response.name: Medical
response.why: Injured crew or sick arrivals reach a clinic within about 1.5 miles (2.5 km).

clearance.name: Border clearance (passport, customs and health checks)
clearance.why: Everyone who comes through a hull door is checked before they reach the public side of the port. Each door needs a clearance point close by, so no one walks a long way unchecked.

must_have.name: One command room for every hull door
must_have.why: Today three offices each open their own doors (Gate Operations, the Harbourmaster and the Stern Harbourmaster). The main way into the ship needs one room that sees every hull door, can lock them all down, and runs the guard.

per_precinct.name: Service shaft to the service layer

military.name: {end} Guard Berth
military.purpose: A secure berth in the hull for the port guard's patrol cutters, military transports and official arrivals. Ships here are met by the guard and cleared on the spot, away from the passenger gates.
military.notes: Planner, 28 Nov 2026: military and government door at the {end_lower} end of the port's hull front

guard_station.name: Port Guard Station
guard_station.purpose: Home of the port guard, the armed security force for the hull doors. Guard crews for the cutters, a ready room, an armoury and a holding area sit beside the guard berths, so the guard can close and hold any door in minutes.

crew.door_note: outer door 6 x 7 ft (1.83 x 2.13 m), the standard double door
crew.name: {pid} Crew Airlocks
crew.purpose: Small airlocks in the hull, one in each pressure zone, so crews, inspectors and suited workers can step outside or come in without opening a ship-sized door. Each is a chamber with a door at each end.

small_craft.note: Planner, 28 Nov 2026: two skiff locks in the hull, 131 ft (40 m) wide, at the thirds of the marina

clearance.name: {where} Border Post
clearance.purpose: A border post beside the docks. Crews and passengers of ships berthed here show their passports, declare goods and are health-checked before they walk into the port, and departing crews are checked out here.

command.name: Port Security Command
command.purpose: The one room that watches every hull door of the port. It sees every gate, berth, lock and airlock, can lock them all down at once, runs the port guard and works with Customs & Border Hq, the harbourmasters and Gate Operations.
command.services_text: Sees and can lock every hull door of the port

fire.name: {where} Fire Post
fire.purpose: A small crash-fire-rescue post close to the far berths, with two rescue appliances and a crew on watch, so a fire or accident at any hull door is reached within about three minutes.

police.name: {where} Guard Post
police.purpose: A small guard post close to the far berths, where port guard officers watch the hull doors nearby and answer calls from the berths within minutes.

medical.name: {where} First Aid Post
medical.purpose: A first aid post close to the far berths, with paramedics, a treatment room and an ambulance bay, for injured crews and sick arrivals before they go on to a clinic.
